Titan to expand jewellery retail footprint to add 150 stores in FY24
Titan Company, which belongs to the Tata Group, says as part of the aggressive retail footprint expansion of its four jewellery brands, it will add another 140 to 150 stores during FY24. Currently, the jewellery vertical has around 750 stores across the country. Titan operates brands including Tanishq, Mia, CaratLane, and Zoya. According to Ajoy Chawla, CEO of the Jewellery Division at Titan Company Ltd, the company added approximately 140 stores last year and plans to add a similar number or potentially even more this year due to promising opportunities. Along with these new stores, Titan will also renovate another 25 of its existing stores this year. The company says the demand environment is good and aims to continue gaining a bigger market share. “We currently hold a market share of 7 per cent of the 32 per cent of the organized market, this has been a steady gain in the share, and going forward we will continue to build on the same,” Chawla said.

In September 1993, Titan Watches changed its name to Titan Industries as it ventured into products other than watches.[15][16] In 1994, Titan launched its jewellery brand Tanishq.[17]
In 1997, Titan and Timex terminated their partnership.[14] In a bid to compete with Timex, Titan soon after launched a range of economy watches under Sonata,[18] and a watch and accessories sub-brand, Fastrack, which was targeted at younger customers.[19]
In 2004, Titan signed an agreement with the Murjani Group to market and distribute the latter's Tommy Hilfiger watches in India.[20] 2004, Titan partnered with LVMH to service the latter's watches in India through its service centres.[21]
In 2005, Fastrack was positioned as an independent accessory brand targeting the urban youth. To become a fashion brand, Fastrack launched sunglasses in the same year and launched bags, belts and wallets in 2009.[22] In 2007, Titan established its prescription eyewear store chain called Titan Eyeplus.[23] Titan launched a multi-brand luxury watch store format called Helios in 2009.[24]

Titan acquired Swiss watchmaker Favre-Leuba in 2011 for €2 million to enter the European market.[25][26] In 2013, Titan entered the fragrances segment with the brand Skinn[27] and helmets category under the Fastrack brand.[28] In the same year, it changed its name to Titan Company Ltd.[29] In 2014, it entered into a joint venture with Montblanc to establish its retail stores in India.[30]
In 2016, Titan entered the wearable devices market by introducing its smartwatch, Juxt, made through a collaboration with Hewlett-Packard.[31] In 2017, the company launched a fitness tracker, named Gesture Band under its youth accessories brand, Fastrack.[32] In 2018, the company added new fitness tracker bands. The company had a 7.4% market share in the wearable devices market as of 2018.[33]
In 2017, Titan started its women's ethnic wear retail chain named Taneira.[34] In 2018, Titan merged its South India-focused jewellery brand Gold Plus with Tanishq.[35]
In November 2020, Titan opened its first overseas Tanishq store in Dubai.[36]
